subject: physics
title: Pressure and pressure in liquids
key_idea: (Separate science) Pressure is force per unit area, **p = F ÷ A**. A fluid pushes at right angles on any surface it touches. In a liquid, pressure increases with depth and with density, **p = h × ρ × g**.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers what pressure is and how to calculate it from a force and an area.

items.meaning: The force acting normally (at right angles) on each unit of area of a surface.
The unit of pressure. One pascal is one newton per square metre (N/m²).

blocks.label: Pressure
where: F is the force normal (at right angles) to the surface in newtons (N).
A is the area of the surface in square metres (m²).

items: The same force on a smaller area gives a larger pressure.
A drawing pin has a pointed tip with a very small area, so the pressure on the wood is large.
The flat head has a large area, so the pressure on the thumb is much less.
The pressure in a fluid causes a force at right angles to any surface.

items.text: A tank bottom of area 0.80 m² has a force of 2400 N on it: p = 2400 ÷ 0.80

diagram.alt: Calculate the pressure that a force exerts on an area.
diagram.question: A force of {F} N acts at right angles on an area of {A} m². Calculate the pressure.

items: Pressure is the force at right angles to a surface divided by the area of the surface.
The same force on a smaller area gives a bigger pressure.
Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa), or N/m².

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers how the pressure in a liquid depends on depth and density.

items: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth.
Pressure at the same depth is greater in a denser liquid.
The weight of the column of liquid above a point pushes down on it.
A deeper point has a taller column above it, so the pressure is greater.

blocks.label: Pressure due to a column of liquid
where: h is the height of the column, or depth, in metres (m).
ρ is the density of the liquid in kilograms per metre cubed (kg/m³).
g is the gravitational field strength in newtons per kilogram (N/kg). The value is given in the question.

items.text: A column 0.5 m tall of liquid of density 1100 kg/m³, with g = 10 N/kg: p = 0.5 × 1100 × 10

blocks.text: To find the increase in pressure between two depths, use the difference in depth for h.

diagram.alt: Change the depth and the liquid and see the pressure due to the liquid.

outputs.label: Pressure due to the liquid (g = 10 N/kg)

items: Pressure in a liquid increases with depth and with density.
p = h × ρ × g gives the pressure due to a column of liquid.
For a change in pressure, use the change in depth.

checks.q: A force of 27 N acts on the bottom of a container of area 0.009 m². Calculate the pressure and give the unit.
Explain why the tip of a drawing pin goes into wood but the head does not go into a thumb.
checks.a: The force is the same at the tip and the head. The tip has a very small area so the pressure is large. The head has a large area so the pressure is much less.

checks.q: The top of a block is 6.6 m below the surface of water of density 1000 kg/m³. g = 10 N/kg. Calculate the pressure on the top of the block.

mistakes.wrong: The unit of pressure is pa.
mistakes.right: Write Pa with a capital P. 'pa' is not accepted. N/m² is also allowed.

mistakes.wrong: A swimmer goes from 0.50 m to 1.70 m, so the pressure increase is 1.70 × 1030 × 9.8.
mistakes.right: Use the increase in depth, 1.70 − 0.50 = 1.2 m. The increase in pressure is 1.2 × 1030 × 9.8 = 12 112.8 Pa.

worked_example.question: A person swims from a depth of 0.50 m to a depth of 1.70 m below the surface of the sea. Density of the sea water = 1030 kg/m³. Gravitational field strength = 9.8 N/kg. Calculate the increase in pressure on the swimmer. Give the unit.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the depth change, the substitution, the answer and the unit. An answer without the unit scores 3 marks.

blocks.text: (Higher tier) In this specification the equation for the pressure due to a column of liquid is Higher tier only. Pressure from force and area is for all students.

exam_phrases: same force at tip and head
pointed end has a very small surface area
at pointed end the pressure is large
flat end has a large surface area
at flat end the pressure is much less

mistakes.wrong: The container is 6.0 m by 2.0 m with weight 15 000 N, so the pressure is 15 000 ÷ 6.0.
mistakes.right: Find the area first: 6.0 × 2.0 = 12 m². Then p = 15 000 ÷ 12 = 1250 Pa, about 1300 Pa. The area is worth a mark.

mistakes.wrong: The force on the ice is 4.8 × 10⁷ × 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ = 576 N.
mistakes.right: The question asks for 2 significant figures. Round 576 N to 580 N. The rounding is the third mark.

mistakes.wrong: The drawing pin goes into the wood because the point is sharper.
mistakes.right: Compare pressures using force and area. The force is the same, the pointed end has a very small area so the pressure is large.

worked_example.question: The bottom of a water tank has an area of 0.80 m². The force on the bottom of the tank, due to the water, is 2400 N. Calculate the pressure, due to the water, on the bottom of the tank.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for recalling the equation, substituting and evaluating. The correct answer without working earns all three marks.

items: The pressure in a fluid is due to the fluid and atmospheric pressure.
10 m of sea water exerts the same pressure as the atmosphere. At a depth of 50 m, the sea water pressure is 5 times atmospheric pressure, so the total is 6 times atmospheric pressure.

exam_phrases: pressure due to a column of liquid = height of column x density of liquid x g

mistakes.wrong: A car weighs 12 000 N and each tyre has an area of 25 cm², so the pressure is 12 000 ÷ 25 = 480 N/cm².
mistakes.right: Four tyres touch the road. The total area is 4 × 25 = 100 cm². The pressure is 12 000 ÷ 100 = 120 N/cm².

mistakes.wrong: The pressure at the bottom of the measuring cylinder is 0.5 × 1100 = 550 Pa.
mistakes.right: Multiply by g as well. p = 0.5 × 1100 × 10 = 5500 Pa.

worked_example.question: Calculate the pressure at the bottom of a 0.5 m tall measuring cylinder filled with a liquid. Density of the liquid = 1100 kg/m³. Use g = 10 N/kg.
answer_points: Pressure due to a column of liquid = height × density × g
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 5500 Pa scores all 3 marks. Using g = 9.8 N/kg and getting 5390 Pa also scores 3 marks.

items: In a simple hydraulic system, a force on one piston creates a pressure in the fluid.
The pressure acts at right angles on the area of another piston, so p = F ÷ A is used on each piston.
A larger area at the second piston gives a larger force.
